faq.a: Talha is associated with the Arabic form طَلْحَة, whose core sense is talha; a tree (acacia).

faq.q: What is the origin of Talha?
faq.a: Talha is associated with Arabic. Talha is Arabic طَلْحَة (Ṭalḥa), a lexical item for a kind of tree. It was borne by a companion of the Prophet.
Yes — the underlying form طَلْحَة is Arabic.
Talha can occur in Muslim naming contexts, but it is better described as a Arabic-origin name used within some Muslim naming traditions than as an exclusively Islamic religious term.
Talha should not be classified as a Quranic personal name without a direct Quranic basis. Ṭalḥa is not a Quranic personal name.

faq.q: What does Talha mean in Urdu?
faq.a: In Urdu, Talha is rendered طلحہ and carries the sense طلحہ، ایک درخت.

faq.q: What does Talha mean in Persian?
faq.a: In Persian, Talha is rendered طلحه and carries the sense طلحه، درختی.
A romanized syllable approximation is tal-ha. No IPA transcription is asserted because a verified phonetic transcription was not available.

faq.q: What are the variants of Talha?
faq.a: Romanization variants include Talha, talha. Script forms are طلحه, طلحہ, طَلْحَة, तलहा.

faq.q: Is Talha a boy's or girl's name?
faq.a: Documented usage records this form as male. Gender is not inferred from the meaning of the word, and actual use may vary between communities.
